summary: Ray-triangle intersection test that produces a ride-height delta. Transforms a triangle vertex (selected from a per-index vertex array on this) into world space using the object's 3x3 orientation matrix and position offset, computes two candidate ray-hit distances (a plane intersection distance and a helper-based distance), takes the larger, clamps it to 0.025, and returns the rest height at this[3371] minus the clamped delta. Returns the unmodified rest height when the intersection is behind the ray or beyond the clamp threshold.

operations.description: Load two input vectors from a2 into locals: v30..v32 from a2+36/40/44 and a second vector from a2+48/52/56, then compute v25 as their dot product.
Select the triangle vertex at this[3758 + 3 * dword(a2+20)] and rotate it by the 3x3 orientation matrix stored at this[3372..3380].
Translate the rotated vertex by the position offset this[3381..3383] to obtain the world-space triangle corner v33..v35.
F_3DCrossProduct(this+3393, v4, &v27) computes a cross product used for the triangle plane, copied into v36..v38.
Vec3Add(this+3390, &v36, v39) sums vectors; the result is copied into v27..v29.
Compute the plane-intersection denominator v14 by rotating v27..v29 through the 3x3 matrix at this[3372..3380] and dotting with the ray direction v30..v32.
If v14 equals 0.0 use a zero distance; otherwise set the first candidate distance v40 = (v35*v32 + v34*v31 + v33*v30 - v25) / v14.
RideHeightDelta(this, &v33) adjusts the candidate triangle corner in place.
Rotate v33..v35 by the 3x3 matrix into v36..v38, then F_3DVectorAddition(&v36, this+3381) applies the position offset.
Second F_3DCrossProduct(this+3393, &v33, v39); the result is copied back into v33..v35.
Second Vec3Add(this+3390, &v33, v39) into v27..v29, then F_33MatrixVectorMultiply(v3, &v27, v39) applies the 3x3 matrix.
sub_4EFEE0 computes two signed distances: v26 = sub_4EFEE0(&v36, &v30) - v25 and v22 = sub_4EFEE0(v39, &v30); the second candidate distance is v23 = v26/v22, or 0.0 when v22 equals 0.0.
Take the maximum of the two candidate distances v40 and v23 as the final ride height delta.
If the delta is negative the ray misses the surface; return the rest height this[3371].
Return rest height minus the clamped delta: this[3371] - v23 when within 0.025, otherwise this[3371] - 0.025.
